title: Je vais partir
intro: The easiest way to talk about the future: **aller** + a verb in the infinitive, exactly like English *I'm going to…*: *je **vais** partir, il **va** pleuvoir*. You already know the forms of aller, so you already know half of it!

cases.label: aller + infinitive
cases.rule: The present of **aller** + an **infinitive**: *je vais manger, tu vas partir, nous allons voir, ils vont venir*. Only **aller** changes.

cases.label: the negative
cases.rule: **ne … pas** goes around **aller**: *je **ne** vais **pas** partir*. Same with *jamais* and *plus*.

cases.label: questions
cases.rule: Raise your voice (*Tu vas venir ?*), or use **est-ce que** / **qu'est-ce que**: *Qu'est-ce que tu vas faire ?*

cases.label: reflexive verbs
cases.rule: The reflexive pronoun goes **just before the infinitive** and matches the subject: *je vais **me** lever, nous allons **nous** promener*.

cases.label: il va pleuvoir
cases.rule: The weather to come: *il va pleuvoir, il va neiger, il va faire beau*. **il y a** becomes **il va y avoir**.

cases.label: demain, la semaine prochaine…
cases.rule: Time words for the future: *demain, ce soir, ce week-end, bientôt, la semaine prochaine, le mois prochain, l'année prochaine, cet été*.

cases.label: dans + time = in
cases.rule: **dans** + a length of time = *in* (from now): *dans deux jours, dans une heure, dans dix minutes*.

cases.label: aller + place or aller + verb
cases.rule: **aller + a place** is the present: *je vais au cinéma*. **aller + a verb** is the future: *je vais regarder un film*. Both together are fine: *je vais aller au cinéma*.

sections.title: 1. aller + infinitive
text: Take the present of **aller** and add a verb in the **infinitive** (the dictionary form: *manger, partir, faire…*). It works just like English *I'm going to…*

examples.fr: {Je vais manger|fp-form} au restaurant ce soir.
examples.en: I'm going to eat at the restaurant tonight.

examples.fr: {Nous allons visiter|fp-form} Montréal.
examples.en: We're going to visit Montréal.

examples.fr: {Ils vont arriver|fp-form} à huit heures.
examples.en: They're going to arrive at eight o'clock.

sections.tip: Only **aller** changes. The second verb stays in the infinitive: *ils vont **partir*** (never *ils vont partent*).

sections.title: 2. The negative
text: **ne … pas** goes around the conjugated verb, **aller**. The infinitive comes after it.

head: French
English
rows: Je ne vais plus manger de pizza.
I'm not going to eat pizza any more.

examples.fr: {Je ne vais pas partir|fp-neg} cet été.
examples.en: I'm not going to go away this summer.

examples.fr: {Elle ne va pas venir|fp-neg} ce soir.
examples.en: She isn't going to come tonight.

examples.fr: {On ne va pas jouer|fp-neg} au foot sous la pluie !
examples.en: We're not going to play football in the rain!

sections.title: 3. Questions

head: French
English
rows: What are you going to do?
Où est-ce que vous allez dormir ?
Where are you going to sleep?
When is he going to arrive?

examples.fr: {Tu vas venir|fp-question} à la fête ?
examples.en: Are you going to come to the party?

examples.fr: {Qu'est-ce que tu vas faire|fp-question} ce week-end ?
examples.en: What are you going to do this weekend?

examples.fr: {Quand est-ce que vous allez partir|fp-question} ?
examples.en: When are you going to leave?

sections.tip: In casual speech the question word can go at the end: *Tu vas faire **quoi** ?*

sections.title: 4. Reflexive verbs
text: With a reflexive verb, the pronoun stays **with the infinitive**, just before it, and it matches the subject.

examples.fr: {Je vais me coucher|fp-reflexive} tôt ce soir.
examples.en: I'm going to go to bed early tonight.

examples.fr: {Tu vas te lever|fp-reflexive} à quelle heure ?
examples.en: What time are you going to get up?

examples.fr: Demain, {nous allons nous promener|fp-reflexive} au parc.
examples.en: Tomorrow, we're going to go for a walk in the park.

sections.tip: In the negative, **ne … pas** still goes around **aller**: *je **ne** vais **pas** me lever*.

sections.title: 5. The weather tomorrow
text: Weather forecasts love the near future. Notice that **il y a** becomes **il va y avoir**.

head: Today
Tomorrow
rows: Il va y avoir du vent.

examples.fr: {Il va pleuvoir|fp-weather} cet après-midi.
examples.en: It's going to rain this afternoon.

examples.fr: Demain, {il va faire beau|fp-weather}.
examples.en: Tomorrow, the weather is going to be nice.

examples.fr: {Il va y avoir un orage|fp-weather} ce soir.
examples.en: There's going to be a storm tonight.

sections.title: 6. Time words for the future

examples.fr: {Demain|fp-time}, je vais faire du sport.
examples.en: Tomorrow, I'm going to do some sport.

examples.fr: {La semaine prochaine|fp-time}, nous allons partir à Paris.
examples.en: Next week, we're going to leave for Paris.

examples.fr: Je vais {bientôt|fp-time} avoir vingt ans.
examples.en: I'm soon going to be twenty.

sections.tip: Short words like **bientôt** often go between **aller** and the infinitive: *je vais bientôt partir*.

sections.title: 7. dans + time = in
text: To say *in* ten minutes, *in* two days (from now), use **dans**.

examples.fr: Le train part {dans dix minutes|fp-dans} !
examples.en: The train leaves in ten minutes!

examples.fr: Je vais finir {dans une heure|fp-dans}.
examples.en: I'm going to finish in an hour.

examples.fr: {Dans deux mois|fp-dans}, nous allons être à Montréal.
examples.en: In two months, we're going to be in Montréal.

sections.tip: Don't use **en** here: *en deux jours* means *within two days* (how long something takes).

sections.title: 8. aller + place or aller + verb?
text: **aller** + a place is simply the present: *je vais au cinéma* (I'm going to the cinema). **aller** + a verb is the near future. You can even use both: *je vais aller au cinéma*.

head: French
English
rows: I'm going to watch a film.
I'm going to go to the cinema.

examples.fr: {Je vais à la piscine|fp-place}.
examples.en: I'm going to the pool.

examples.fr: {Je vais nager|fp-place}.
examples.en: I'm going to swim.

examples.fr: Samedi, {je vais aller|fp-place} à la plage.
examples.en: On Saturday, I'm going to go to the beach.

sections.tip: *Je vais aller…* may look odd, but it's perfectly normal French.

mistakes.why: The second verb stays in the infinitive.
No **à** between aller and the infinitive.
The reflexive pronoun goes just before the infinitive.

mistakes.wrong: en deux jours (= two days from now)

story.title: Les projets de l'été
story.en: At the café downstairs, everyone talks about their summer plans.

lines.fr: Il fait beau. Léa, Sophie, Hugo et Tom prennent un café au café d'en bas.
lines.en: The weather's nice. Léa, Sophie, Hugo and Tom are having a coffee at the café downstairs.

lines.fr: {Qu'est-ce que vous allez faire|fp-question} cet été ?
lines.en: What are you going to do this summer?

lines.fr: {Dans deux mois|fp-dans}, {nous allons partir|fp-form} à Montréal : mes parents, Lou et moi !
lines.en: In two months, we're going to leave for Montréal: my parents, Lou and me!

lines.fr: On va voir mon cousin Antoine, et {on va se promener|fp-reflexive} dans la ville.
lines.en: We're going to see my cousin Antoine, and we're going to walk around the city.

lines.fr: Moi, {je vais à Madrid|fp-place} avec Inès. {On va visiter|fp-form} la ville et {on va danser|fp-form} tous les soirs !
lines.en: Me, I'm going to Madrid with Inès. We're going to visit the city and we're going to dance every night!

lines.fr: Et toi, Hugo ? Tu pars à Montréal avec ta famille ?
lines.en: And you, Hugo? Are you going to Montréal with your family?

lines.fr: En juillet, {je ne vais pas partir|fp-neg} : je dois travailler. Mais {je vais aller|fp-place} à Montréal en août !
lines.en: In July, I'm not going to go away: I have to work. But I'm going to go to Montréal in August!

lines.fr: Hugo, {tu ne vas pas oublier|fp-neg} ton passeport, d'accord ?
lines.en: Hugo, you're not going to forget your passport, OK?

lines.fr: Mais non ! Et {je vais me lever|fp-reflexive} tôt pour l'avion, promis !
lines.en: Of course not! And I'm going to get up early for the plane, I promise!

lines.fr: {Il va arriver|fp-form} en retard, c'est sûr…
lines.en: He's going to be late, that's for sure…

lines.fr: Moi, {je vais rentrer|fp-form} en Angleterre {la semaine prochaine|fp-time}, pour voir ma famille.
lines.en: I'm going to go back to England next week, to see my family.

lines.fr: Et en Angleterre, {il va faire beau|fp-weather} ?
lines.en: And in England, is the weather going to be nice?
No! It's going to rain, of course!

lines.fr: À Madrid, {il va faire très chaud|fp-weather} : quarante degrés !
lines.en: In Madrid, it's going to be very hot: forty degrees!

lines.fr: Regardez le ciel… {Il va y avoir un orage|fp-weather} ! Vite, on rentre !
lines.en: Look at the sky… There's going to be a storm! Quick, let's go inside!

lines.fr: Pas de panique, Hugo : on va {bientôt|fp-time} être à la maison. Le café d'en bas, c'est sous notre appartement !
lines.en: Don't panic, Hugo: we'll soon be home. The café downstairs is right under our flat!

quiz.q: Nous ___ visiter Montréal.
Ils vont ___ ce soir.
quiz.en: They're going to arrive this evening.
quiz.why: After **aller**, the verb stays in the infinitive.

quiz.q: How do you say “I'm going to eat”?
How do you say “I'm not going to leave”?
Elle ne ___ pas venir ce soir.
quiz.en: She isn't going to come tonight.

quiz.q: Qu'est-ce que tu ___ faire ce week-end ?
quiz.en: What are you going to do this weekend?

quiz.q: Est-ce que vous ___ venir ?
Je vais ___ coucher tôt.
quiz.en: I'm going to go to bed early.

quiz.q: Nous allons ___ promener au parc.
quiz.en: We're going to go for a walk in the park.

quiz.q: How do you say “I'm going to get up”?
How do you say “It's going to rain”?
Demain, il va ___ beau.
quiz.en: Tomorrow, the weather is going to be nice.

quiz.q: Ce soir, il va ___ un orage.
quiz.en: There's going to be a storm tonight.

quiz.q: « bientôt » means…
L'année ___, je vais aller au Canada.
quiz.en: Next year, I'm going to go to Canada.

quiz.q: Which one is in the future?
How do you say “in two days” (from now)?
Le train part ___ dix minutes.
quiz.en: The train leaves in ten minutes.

quiz.q: « Je vais nager » means…
« Je vais à la piscine » means…
Can you say « Je vais aller à Paris » ?
options: yes: I'm going to go to Paris
no: you can't use aller twice
quiz.answer: yes: I'm going to go to Paris
